tutorial.text: The header guides you through each step of the tutorial and tasks. Use the Frontiers panel to toggle which frontiers are loaded. Across all charts, solutions are separated by frontier; charts that support it offer a Frontier Colours option to colour-code them. The Chart Guide is your cheatsheet; open it at any point if you need a reminder of chart interactions.

The tool has two linked spaces. The Objectives Space shows your output metrics (y = f(x)). The Decision Space shows the allocations (x) that produce them. Each point is a solution on the Pareto frontier, representing an optimal trade-off.

Every chart supports hovering, selection, and filtering. Hold Shift + click a point to select it; selections are synchronized between both spaces. Click the zoom in/out button to zoom in/out. Use Clear Selection to reset any active filter.
Both spaces offer several visualisation types. We'll walk through each one, explaining their functionality.

The 2D Scatterplot shows the relationship between two objectives. Use the axis dropdowns to change what's plotted. Shift + click to select a point, or use the Lasso Tool to select an area. Click Options to customise: Dim. Reduction projects all objectives into 2D via PCA, Labels shows solution IDs on each point, and Dominant Allocation colours points by their largest allocation group.

The 3D Scatterplot adds a third axis; click and drag to rotate. Click Options for extras: Surface renders the Pareto frontier as a mesh, Dominated shows non-optimal solutions, and Ideal Point marks the theoretical best.

The Parallel Coordinates Plot draws each objective as a vertical axis; each solution is a line crossing all axes. Brush (click and drag) an axis to filter to a range; deselect by double-clicking it or using Clear Selection. Drag an axis by its label to reorder axes. Click Options to colour lines by Dominant Allocation.

The Radar Chart maps each objective onto a radial axis; each solution is a polygon. Brush (click and drag) an axis to filter; deselect by double-clicking it or using Clear Selection. Drag an axis by its label to reorder axes. Click Options to colour polygons by Dominant Allocation.

RadViz positions solutions around a circle of objective anchors; balanced solutions sit near the centre, objective-dominated ones are pulled towards their anchor. Shift + click or use the Lasso Tool to select. Each solution is a mini pie glyph: click to expand into a donut chart, click a group arc to drill into individual allocations, and click the centre area to close. Use Options to toggle Spread (grid layout).

The Correlation Heatmap shows pairwise correlations between objectives. Dark = negative correlation; light = positive. When multiple frontiers are loaded, a separate heatmap is shown for each, so you can compare correlation patterns across frontiers.

The Column Chart shows decision variable values as grouped bars, one bar per solution. Shift + click a bar to select that solution. Frontiers are grouped and labelled with a bracket and name above their columns. Some categories represent allocation groups: click a group bar to expand it and see individual allocations, which also expands the section in the tooltip.

The Table lists every solution with raw objective and decision values. Sort by any column. The mini bars at the top show the distribution per frontier; Brush (click and drag) to filter to a range, deselect by double-clicking or using Clear Selection. Allocation group columns can be expanded to show individual allocations.
